[{'id': 1, 'slug': 'abbey-villa', 'name': 'Abbey Villa', 'shortName': 'Villa', 'badge': 'abbey-villa.png', 'division': 'Premier Division', 'location': 'Millisle', 'founded': 1955, 'ground': 'Adams Park', 'primaryColour': '#800000', 'secondaryColour': '#87CEEB', 'website': None, 'twitter': None, 'facebook': 'Abbey Villa FC', 'instagram': None, 'about': 'In 1955, the late Thomas Waugh, the Bennett brothers (Nelson, Tom, Raymond and Norman), and others formed a village team, Millisle United, in the Cardy League. They soon progressed to the Churches League as Millisle Presbyterian, with a second team in the Belfast Minor League, and finally arrived on the Northern Amateur League scene in 1962.

The club reached the IFA Junior Cup final in 1988 and won the Clarence Cup in 1990/91 while still a Second Division team. The current ground, Adams Park, and the Waugh Pavilion were officially opened in August 1992 when Villa beat Irish League club Ards 2–0, and the club enjoyed a memorable season. Now an intermediate club, Villa won the Border Regiment Cup in 1992, won 1B by an 11-point margin, reached the last 16 of the Irish Cup, and earned the Best Junior Team award.

Between 2008 and 2011, brothers Graham and Mark Bailie led the first team as the club again won the Border Regiment Cup, reached the last 16 of the IFA Irish Challenge Cup, were named ‘Junior Team of the Year’ by the Football Writers Association, and won promotion to the NAFL Premier Division. In 2012, the club opened a 70m x 30m 3G training facility and new changing rooms, supporting major growth in the youth set-up.

In 2024/25, the first team, managed by Scott Collins, won Division 1A to gain promotion to the NAFL Premier Division, while Nikki Caskey’s second team won Division 3B and also lifted the Walter Moore Cup. Former youth player Mason Munn made his debut for Glasgow Rangers in January, and club member Conrad Kirkwood served as Irish FA President from 2021 to 2026.

The club’s motto, “Semper Ad Meliora” (“Always towards better things”), reflects its ambitions on and off the pitch and in the community.
